Description: Valentina Doria, daughter of Genoese Ghibelline leader Bernabò Doria, was the wife of Stefano Visconti. Reared in naval royalty, she channeled maritime wealth and credit to Milan, raising three future sovereign rulers—Matteo II, Galeazzo II, and Barnabò—with maternal iron. Lady Valentina scrutinized ducal rent-rolls and salt monopolies with sharp Genoese precision, subjecting her three sons to severe martial training to prepare them for absolute dominion over northern Italy. Capitalizing upon her kinship with the naval rulers of Genoa, she secured armed maritime escorts during blockades, establishing unshakeable merchant credit for Visconti enterprises across Europe. Proud and unbending, this Genoese matriarch insisted that iron maternal discipline and commercial credit alone conquered destiny, molding her three sons into sovereigns of northern Italy. Throughout every bitter factional siege, imperial diet, and shifting territorial campaign across Lombardy, their relentless aristocratic dedication, strategic statecraft, chivalric discipline, steadfast valor, and immense personal resources preserve the sovereign dignity, mercantile wealth, and military supremacy of the Lordship of Milan, safeguarding civic liberty, territorial integrity, and Visconti dynastic grandeur against every rival commune, papal coalition, and hostile league across the Po valley and northern Italy for future generations to inherit with pride, commanding profound imperial reverence from all subjects throughout Christendom.
Motivations: Elevate her three sons to undisputed supreme lordship over the Milanese domain.
Preserve naval trade monopolies between Genoa and Milan for mutual enrichment.
Impose Genoese mercantile bookkeeping upon ducal manors to eradicate embezzlements.
Values: Believes supreme statecraft must be anchored in limitless gold and dynastic pedigree.
Regards maternal protection as sacred, striking down any threat to her sons without pity.
Fears: Her three sons turning against one another in fratricidal wars for absolute control.
Guelf coups in Genoa severing the naval sanctuaries of her native House Doria.
SpeechStyle: Speaks with icy composure and commercial sharpness, projecting Genoese patrician pride. Always fiercely defending Visconti dynastic authority, Milanese civic grandeur, and Lombard territorial hegemony.
